svg.text: The real (Einstein–Hilbert) flow: every trajectory spirals out of one fixed point, then runs to classical gravity
λ = Λ/k² (cosmological constant in probe units)
g = G k²
fixed point (0.707, 0.193)
Gaussian point
λ = ½
Reproduced (check A6): the optimised-cutoff
fixed point and exponents θ = 1.475 ± 3.043 i.
Complex θ means the flow into the fixed point
both shrinks and turns: z → e^(−θt) z (A8).
That is e and i together (reading ours).
Leaving the fixed point toward low energy,
each trajectory ends where g·λ = GΛ is
constant: its label is the g-dials number
GħΛ/c³ (A9; Reuter–Weyer 2004).
Blue: Λ < 0. Orange: Λ > 0 (these hit the
λ = ½ wall unless tuned close to the
separatrix, as our universe's must be).
Purple: near the separatrix.
Flow equations: Reuter–Saueressig form with the Litim cutoff, d = 4; truncated, and fixed-point values depend on the scheme.
